column2: New DNA evidence exculpated the farmer, who had spent years under suspicion for the fire.
column3: 新的DNA證據證明那位農夫清白，他多年來一直因那場火災而受到懷疑。
column4: exculpate the accused (證明被告清白)
column5: ex 出去 + culp 過錯，把過錯趕出去就是脫罪

column2: The priest absolved the repentant thief, telling him his past wrongs were forgiven.
column3: 神父赦免了悔過的小偷，告訴他過去的過錯已被原諒。
column5: ab 離開 + solve 解開，把罪的繩結解開

column2: Years later, newly found letters vindicated the scientist's once-ridiculed theory.
column3: 多年後新發現的信件證明了這位科學家曾被嘲笑的理論是正確的。
column4: vindicate a theory (證明理論正確)
column5: Vin 像「聞的剋」，被冤枉的人終於贏回清白

column2: The ledger found in his desk incriminated the manager, linking him directly to the missing funds.
column3: 在他書桌裡找到的帳本使經理涉案，直接把他與失蹤的資金連在一起。
column5: in 裡面 + crimin 罪，把人拉進罪裡面

column2: Prosecutors tried to inculpate the clerk by pointing to his signature on the forged form.
column3: 檢察官指著偽造表格上的簽名，試圖指控這名職員有罪。
column4: inculpate a suspect (指控嫌犯有罪)
column5: in 放進 + culp 過錯，把過錯放到某人身上

column2: The inspector judged the owner culpable for ignoring repeated warnings about the cracked bridge.
column3: 檢查員認定屋主因無視裂橋的多次警告而有過失。
column5: culp 像「可怕」，做錯事要負責才可怕

column2: Her audacious plan to cross the desert alone astonished even the veteran explorers.
column3: 她獨自橫越沙漠的大膽計畫連資深探險家都感到驚訝。
column5: audio 聲音大，敢大聲說敢做就是大膽

column2: He had the temerity to interrupt the judge and demand a different verdict.
column3: 他竟冒失地打斷法官，要求改判不同的結果。
column4: have the temerity to (竟敢冒失地)
column5: 「踢沒力踢」，不自量力亂踢就是魯莽

column2: The insolent apprentice laughed at his master's advice and walked out without a bow.
column3: 那個傲慢的學徒嘲笑師傅的建議，連鞠躬都沒有就走了出去。
column5: in 不 + solent 習慣，不守規矩的態度

column2: With a brazen smile, the senator denied the charge while holding the stolen documents.
column3: 參議員手裡拿著贓物文件，還厚著臉皮笑著否認指控。
column5: brass 黃銅臉皮厚得像銅牆，不怕被看見

column2: The intrepid mountaineer pressed on through the blizzard, undeterred by the unmapped ridge ahead.
column3: 那位無畏的登山者不顧暴風雪繼續前進，也不怕前方未標示的山稜。
column5: in 不 + trep 顫抖，腳不發抖的人

column2: Dauntless in the face of ridicule, the young inventor kept testing her flying machine.
column3: 面對嘲笑，這位年輕發明家毫不退縮，持續測試她的飛行器。
column5: 「當它」不嚇倒的 less，沒有被嚇倒的樣子

column2: The craven general fled the field at the first sound of drums, leaving his soldiers behind.
column3: 那位怯懦的將軍一聽到鼓聲就逃離戰場，把士兵拋在身後。
column5: 「磕碰」到小事就縮起來的膽小鬼

column2: The timorous kitten hid beneath the sofa whenever the doorbell rang.
column3: 門鈴一響，那隻膽小的小貓就躲到沙發底下。
column5: 「踢摸蕊」，輕輕一踢就嚇得縮起來

column2: Though gifted, he was too diffident to share his poems with anyone but his sister.
column3: 他雖有天分，卻太缺乏自信，只肯把詩拿給妹妹看。
column5: dif 離開 + fid 信任，離開自信就會害羞

column2: The pusillanimous committee, afraid of criticism, postponed every decision until the crisis had passed.
column3: 那個怯懦的委員會因害怕批評，把每項決定都拖到危機過去。
column5: puss 小貓 + anim 心，小貓的心膽子小

column2: The erudite professor effortlessly quoted Latin poets, medieval chronicles, and modern physics in a single lecture.
column3: 這位博學的教授在一堂課中輕鬆引用拉丁詩人、中世紀編年史與現代物理。
column5: e 出 + rud 粗魯，把粗魯磨掉就成了博學

column2: A learned judge, she cited cases from three centuries to support her ruling.
column3: 她是一位博學的法官，引用三個世紀的案例來支持她的判決。
column5: learn 加 ed 讀成兩音節，讀很多書才有學問

column2: His pedantic corrections of every comma bored the audience and obscured his actual argument.
column3: 他對每個逗號都吹毛求疵的糾正讓聽眾厭煩，也掩蓋了他真正的論點。
column5: pedal 一腳一腳踩，死板地一格一格計較

column2: A true polymath, Leonardo painted masterpieces, designed machines, and studied anatomy with equal brilliance.
column3: 達文西是真正的通才，畫出傑作、設計機器、研究解剖，樣樣出色。
column5: poly 很多 + math 數學學問，樣樣都懂的人

column2: The film's didactic ending, with its obvious moral lecture, felt more like a classroom than a story.
column3: 這部電影說教式的結局帶著明顯的道德訓話，感覺更像課堂而非故事。
column5: 「大得」想教你，滿口大道理的老師

column2: Visiting the village school was an edifying experience that reminded the visitors what real dedication looks like.
column3: 造訪那所鄉村學校是一次啟迪人心的經驗，讓訪客想起真正的奉獻是什麼樣子。
column5: edi 像 edit 編輯，把心靈修好修正

column2: Dogmatic about her diet, she dismissed every study that contradicted her fixed beliefs.
column3: 她對自己的飲食方式非常武斷，駁回每一項與她既定信念相反的研究。
column5: dog 狗咬著骨頭不放，堅持己見不鬆口

column2: Doctrinaire planners ignored the farmers' complaints and applied the theory exactly as written.
column3: 教條主義的規劃者無視農民的抱怨，完全照著理論字面套用。
column5: doctrine 教義 + aire，只認書上的條文

column2: An iconoclast by nature, the young painter shattered every rule of traditional portraiture.
column3: 那位年輕畫家天生是打破傳統的人，推翻了傳統肖像畫的每一條規則。
column4: artistic iconoclast (藝術界的反傳統者)
column5: icon 聖像 + clast 打破，把偶像砸掉的人

column2: The party's maverick, he voted against his leaders whenever his conscience demanded it.
column3: 他是黨內的特立獨行者，只要良心要求，就投票反對自己的領導人。
column5: Maverick 原是不烙印的小牛，不跟牛群走

column2: Centuries ago, the astronomer was branded a heretic for claiming the Earth orbited the sun.
column3: 幾世紀前，那位天文學家因主張地球繞著太陽轉而被視為異端。
column5: here 在這裡 + tic，提出不一樣的想法被貼標籤

column2: The chef's unorthodox method of baking bread in a clay pot surprised even seasoned bakers.
column3: 主廚用陶罐烤麵包的非傳統方法連資深烘焙師都感到意外。
column5: un 不 + ortho 正確 + dox 想法，不是正統想法

column2: Surrounded by sycophants, the king never heard a single honest word about his failing economy.
column3: 國王被一群馬屁精包圍，從未聽到一句關於他衰敗經濟的真話。
column5: 「洗可方」，洗得乾乾淨淨只會捧上司

column2: The obsequious waiter bowed so deeply and so often that the guests felt embarrassed.
column3: 那位卑躬屈膝的服務生鞠躬又深又頻繁，讓客人感到尷尬。
column5: ob 向著 + sequ 跟隨，跟在人屁股後面

column2: The star received such constant adulation that she began to believe she could never make mistakes.
column3: 這位明星受到持續不斷的盲目奉承，因而開始相信自己不會犯錯。
column5: ad 向 + ul 像 wolf 搖尾巴，狗搖尾巴討好

column2: His fawning praise of the director fooled no one, since he had criticized her all week.
column3: 他對導演的奉承誰都騙不過，因為他整個星期都在批評她。
column5: fawn 是小鹿，也像小狗搖尾巴討好主人

column2: She refused to toady to the board, even though agreeing with them would have secured her promotion.
column3: 即使附和董事會就能保住升遷，她仍拒絕諂媚他們。
column4: toady to the boss (向上司諂媚)
column5: toad 是蟾蜍，癩蛤蟆跳到老闆腳邊討好

column2: Aloof at parties, he stood near the window and spoke to no one all evening.
column3: 他在派對上很疏離，整晚站在窗邊，不和任何人說話。
column5: a 一個人 + loof 像 loop，遠遠繞開人群

column2: A good referee must remain detached, judging each foul by the rules rather than by loyalty.
column3: 好裁判必須保持超然，依規則而非忠誠來判定每次犯規。
column5: de 分開 + tach 貼上，把自己撕下來置身事外

column2: Because the arbitrator had no money invested in either company, she was truly disinterested.
column3: 由於仲裁者在兩家公司都沒有投資，她真正是公正無私的。
column5: dis 沒有 + interest 利益，和自己沒利害關係

column2: An impartial jury must weigh the testimony without favoring the plaintiff or the defendant.
column3: 公正的陪審團必須不偏袒原告或被告，衡量證詞。
column5: im 不 + part 一部分，不站在任何一邊

column2: The heirs agreed on an equitable split of the estate, giving each child a fair share.
column3: 繼承人同意以公平合理的方式分割遺產，讓每個孩子都得到公平的一份。
column5: equi 相等 + table 桌子，大家在桌上平等分

column2: The critic's prejudiced review revealed that he had judged the film before ever watching it.
column3: 影評人帶偏見的評論顯示他在看電影之前就已先下判斷。
column5: pre 先 + judge 判斷，還沒看就先判斷

column2: The partisan crowd cheered every claim from their own candidate and booed all opposing views.
column3: 黨派色彩濃厚的群眾對自家候選人的每項主張歡呼，對所有反對意見喝倒采。
column5: party 派對 + san，只挺自己那一隊
